a.d: Action verbs take -는다니 (batchim) or -ㄴ다니 (no batchim) in the present tense (먹는다니, 떠난다니).
ex: 내일 외국으로 **떠난다니** 정말 아쉬워요. — To think you are leaving for abroad tomorrow, I'm so sad.

b.d: Descriptive adjectives take -다니 directly without inserting -ㄴ/는- (예쁘다니, 바쁘다니, 크다니).
ex: 가격이 그렇게 **비싸다니** 깜짝 놀랐어요. — To think the price is so expensive, I was shocked.

im-03-02-02.tip: Verbs insert -ㄴ/는- (간다니, 먹는다니). Adjectives attach directly (좋다니, 예쁘다니). Nouns take -(이)라니.

a.d: Used when directly experiencing something through bodily senses right in the moment (tasting, touching, seeing).
ex: 직접 마셔 보니 커피가 정말 **맛있네요**! — Having tasted it myself, the coffee is really delicious!

b.d: Used when understanding a situation or realizing a fact upon hearing someone's explanation ('Aha, so that's why!').
ex: 설명을 듣고 보니 그런 깊은 뜻이 **있었군요**! — Having heard the explanation, there was such deep meaning!

a.d: Used with friends or peers to gently bring up a shared fact that both parties already know.
ex: 우리 지난주에 같이 갔던 카페 **있잖아**. — You know that cafe we visited together last week.

b.d: When used toward elders or bosses, it easily sounds like 'I already told you, why don't you know?!' (accusatory).
ex: 제가 미리 말씀드렸**잖아요**! (✕ Can sound disrespectful and irritable)

im-03-02-04.tip: Use -잖아요 freely with close friends; when addressing superiors, prefer courteous statements like 미리 말씀드렸습니다.
